lines.t: In one war, the army's best gas alarm wasn't a machine. It was a garden slug.
A scientist at a museum noticed something weird in his basement. When fumes leaked from the furnace, the slugs down there scrunched up tight.
So he goes to the army. Your soldiers need slugs.
Slugs? We have gas masks, professor. Go back to your garden.
The scientist stays calm. A slug in a jar. A tiny bit of mustard gas. So little no soldier can smell it.
The slug squeezes into a ball.
Even less gas. Squeeze. The laughing stops.
You see, a slug breathes through one little hole in its side. When the air turns bad, it shuts the hole and squeezes tight.
It's a smoke alarm... that crawls. And it smells the gas about three times better than a human nose.
And it doesn't even get hurt. It just closes up, waits, and crawls on.
So the army takes the slugs to the trenches. Officially. A five-month tour of duty.
Soldiers watch them in the dark. One night, a slug starts to shrink. Nobody smells a thing.
And the gas rolls in over masks that are already on.
The soldiers who laughed at the slugs... now check their slug before their rifle.
Slug or dog, which one would you trust with your life? A, the slug. Or B, the dog.
